Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was excited by the latency numbers. We chatted internally and would like to put together a short Mutual Action Plan so we can lock the pilot timeline and understand what a committed tranche would look like.

Key asks up front:
- Target pilot start: July 6 (2-4 week pilot)
- Expected peak inference QPS for pilot: ~120 QPS (text-gen, average prompt length 380 tokens)
- Production target after pilot (P0): 600 QPS steady, spikes to 1,200 QPS
- Need clarity on Dedicated -> Private lead times and whether staging can be on shared infra initially

I attached an initial capacity profile and a toy MAP spreadsheet to this thread (meridian_map_v1.xlsx, initial_capacity_profile.csv). Could you confirm typical lead times for Dedicated Dedicated GPU pool provisioning and for a private VPC package (including SOC2 artifacts)? We also have a SOC2 gap assessment we may share — Sam is copied.

We'd like a short mutual plan with milestones we can show the execs (POC kickoff, acceptance criteria, procurement date to lock a tranche). Ideal to get that in the next 5 business days.

Cheers,
Alice Chen

Alice — great to hear you want to move fast. Below is a proposed MAP we can run next week and an initial sizing note based on your profile. I pulled in Ben (Capacity & Onboarding) and Lauren (Solutions) to validate lead times and acceptance gates.

Proposed high-level MAP (timeline+owner):
1) MAP draft and acceptance (this thread) — owner: Mina — target: Tue 2026-05-26
2) Pilot environment (shared hosted) provisioning & test harness — owner: Redwood infra — target: 2026-06-15
3) Pilot kickoff (2 weeks baseline) — owner: Meridian/Redwood ops — target: 2026-07-06
4) Acceptance test run & quality evals (prompts we exchange) — owner: Solutions — target: 2026-07-20
5) Procurement decision & tranche lock (Dedicated pool or Private) — owner: Meridian procurement/Redwood sales — target: 2026-07-27

Sizing notes (initial):
- Pilot: 4 x A100-like slots with autoscaling to 6 for spike headroom (estimated steady cost baseline) — supports ~100–140 QPS given your average token patterns with Redwood batching and KV cache.
- Prod P0 (600 QPS): expect ~20 GPU-equivalent slots (H100-style equivalence) and ability to burst to 35 for spikes. Exact quantity depends on quantization and sequence length distribution; we'll run a short profiling eval during the pilot.

Lead time guidance (ballpark):
- Hosted pilot environment: 2–3 business days for config + infra hooks
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved tranche): 6–8 weeks from signed PO to full capacity for custom tranche with procurement + hardware allocation in our US region
- Private (VPC + on-prem option with SOC2 review): 10–14 weeks — includes KMS integration and SOC2 artifact handoff window

Next steps I need from you by 2026-05-24:
- Confirm pilot acceptance criteria (latency/throughput and SLOs)
- Share top-20 prompts and a small eval set (we can redact PII)
- Procurement lead contact for the procurement milestone

I'll attach a cleaned MAP template and SOC2 request checklist; Ben will follow up on tranche commitment terms.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Capacity Programs, Redwood Inference

Adding procurement/ops notes.

Meridian — a couple of practical asks to make the tranche lock predictable:
- If you plan to lock a Dedicated tranche with a Q3 start, we recommend a signed PO + 50% deposit to secure GPU bucket allocation; without that our next available tranche may slip 4+ weeks depending on vendor lead times.
- For Private/VPC we require a short security intake (SOC2 artifact exchange + network design) and a staging acceptance window for KMS. That path is more prescriptive but gives you the most isolation. Expect a 10–14 week calendar timeline after initial acceptance of SOW.
- We'll run a short profiling sweep during the pilot (2–3 days) that will produce a finalized GPU-equivalent recommendation and a cost estimate. That will be used to size the PO.

Operational fallbacks we recommend:
1) Staged tranches: lock a conservative tranche that covers average expected throughput and leave a 20% burst buffer for the first 3 months.
2) Hybrid rollout: start on hosted with a reserved dedicated tranche queued so you can flip to Dedicated quickly once the PO is processed.

Irene — can you confirm the standard tranche deposit cadence and whether we can accelerate H100-equivalent slots for Meridian if they sign by July 1?

— Ben
